papers.title: Are infraslow oscillations the missing link between sleep and Alzheimer's?
papers.journal: Alzheimer's & dementia : the journal of the Alzheimer's Association
papers.summary: The study analyzed non-REM sleep EEG data from Alzheimer's disease (AD) patients and controls, finding reduced infraslow oscillation (ISO) peak amplitude in AD while frequency and bandwidth were preserved. ISO bandwidth was positively associated with neurofilament light chain (NfL), suggesting ISO weakening may link sleep microarchitecture to AD pathology.

papers.title: CORSICA: Reproducible suppression of cochlear implant artifacts in EEG evoked by continuous speech.
papers.summary: The paper presents CORSICA, a reproducible method for suppressing cochlear implant artifacts in EEG during continuous speech, using ICA components and correlation with the stimulus. It effectively removed artifacts with only 2% of components rejected and enabled recovery of physiologically plausible temporal response functions.

papers.title: Cortical layer 6b mediates state-dependent changes in brain activity and effects of orexin on waking and sleep.
papers.summary: The study silenced cortical layer 6b (L6b) neurons in mice and recorded EEG, finding slowed theta frequency during wake and REM sleep and reduced total EEG power, especially in NREM sleep. L6b silencing also altered the response to orexin infusion, indicating a role in state-dependent brain oscillations.

papers.title: EEG Biomarkers for Affective Disorders Diagnosis: An Evaluation and Validation Study.
papers.summary: The paper introduces 25 commonly used EEG features across four domains and evaluates their diagnostic utility for affective disorders using two resting-state datasets, identifying biomarkers with strong discriminative power. It also discusses key issues in EEG-based diagnosis and biomarker integration.

papers.title: An Intraoperative EEG Biomarker for Postoperative Delirium Predicting Based on Interpretable Deep Learning Framework.
papers.summary: Using interpretable deep learning on intraoperative EEG from 71 older patients, the study identified a frontal EEG biomarker (2-12 Hz oscillations) that predicted postoperative delirium with high accuracy (AUC 0.911). External validation confirmed generalizability, supporting objective intraoperative risk stratification.

papers.title: Semantic predictability selectively modulates delta-band syntax tracking: evidence for good-enough parsing
papers.summary: Reanalyzing an EEG dataset during audiobook listening, the study modeled four syntactic constructs with delta-band temporal response functions and found that semantic dissimilarity selectively modulated responses to syntactic surprisal and closing-node count, but not integration cost. This supports good-enough parsing, showing graded reliance on syntax.

papers.title: Reduced EEG Complexity and Its Association with Social Communication in Adults with Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Multiscale Entropy Study
papers.summary: In adults with autism spectrum disorder (ASD), EEG multiscale entropy (MSE) at longer scales was reduced compared to controls across rest and movie conditions, and this reduction was associated with higher ADOS-2 Social Affect scores. Event-related MSE changes also showed attenuated differentiation between social and non-social windows in ASD.

papers.title: Heterogeneity of Brain Dynamics in Genetic and Psychiatric Conditions
papers.summary: This preprint analyzes resting-state EEG from 4,812 individuals across psychiatric conditions and genetic variants, establishing normative developmental trajectories. It finds psychiatric conditions show small transdiagnostic deviations, while rare genetic variants have larger distinct signatures, and provides an open resource for benchmarking.

papers.title: Noninvasive and objective near-real-time detection of pain changes during tonic fluctuating noxious heat stimulation.
papers.summary: This study trained deep learning models on physiological signals (EEG, electrodermal activity, heart rate, pupil diameter, facial expressions) to detect pain decreases during tonic fluctuating noxious heat in 42 healthy participants. Combining electrodermal activity, heart rate, and pupil diameter achieved optimal classification (AUC=0.854, accuracy=76.8%), with electrodermal activity being the most informative signal, enabling near-real-time detection of spontaneous pain changes.

papers.title: Functional network reorganization and thalamocortical gating as neurobiological markers of recovery in somatic symptom disorder: A 6-month longitudinal source EEG study.
papers.summary: In a 6-month longitudinal source EEG study of patients with somatic symptom disorder (SSD), persistent deficits in gamma-band global efficiency were found, while thalamic spectral power showed significant group-by-time interactions. Symptomatic relief was associated with nodal efficiency reorganization in the left central sensorimotor region (beta band), suggesting multilayered neurobiological architecture.

papers.title: Brain-wide reconfiguration of burst firing by psilocybin reveals 5-HT2A-dependent circuit dynamics
papers.summary: Using simultaneous multi-region Neuropixels recordings in 35 mice, this preprint found that psilocybin selectively reconfigures burst firing, not mean firing rates, across cortex, thalamus, and hippocampus. These burst effects were largely abolished by ketanserin, indicating 5-HT2A receptor dependence.

papers.title: Quantitative EEG-Based Detection of Poststroke Delirium Endotypes and Their Association With Biomarkers of Inflammation.
papers.summary: In a prospective cohort of 87 acute stroke/TIA patients, quantitative EEG (qEEG) metrics detected poststroke delirium with AUC=0.892, and connectivity alterations correlated with inflammatory biomarkers, suggesting qEEG may characterize delirium endotypes. Findings need validation.

papers.title: EEG-Derived Wavelet Index for Assessment of Procedural Sedation in Children Undergoing Magnetic Resonance Examination: A Diagnostic Study.
papers.summary: This prospective diagnostic study compared the wavelet index (WLI) with the Ramsay Sedation Score (RS) for assessing procedural sedation depth in 74 children undergoing MRI. WLI showed superior predictive performance for sedation failure with an AUC of 0.902 versus 0.734 for RS, suggesting WLI may aid risk stratification.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence for Improving the Management of People With Epilepsy in Low-and-Middle Income Countries.
papers.summary: This review examines three AI-based applications for epilepsy management in low- and middle-income countries: a smartphone diagnostic tool, an automated EEG interpretation system (SCORE-AI), and a wearable seizure detector. These tools demonstrated high performance (AUCs 0.89-0.96, sensitivity 85-97.5%), but implementation faces challenges including infrastructure, literacy, ethics, and regulatory issues.

papers.title: Perceived Time Shapes Physical Fatigue Accumulation and Its Neural Oscillatory Correlates.
papers.summary: This study investigated whether perceived time influences physical fatigue accumulation using a novel EEG design with time deception in 24 participants performing isometric contractions. Results showed slowed fatigue accumulation when the clock was slowed down, with frontal oscillatory dynamics tracking perceived rather than actual time.

papers.title: Higher signal diversity, network dysregulation, and increased well-being under DMT administration: An EEG study.
papers.summary: This EEG study in 13 healthy participants found that intravenous DMT reduced connectivity and network efficiency, but increased signal complexity (Higuchi fractal dimension, permutation entropy) in beta/gamma bands. DMT increased beta-to-alpha ratio and frontal alpha asymmetry, correlating with subjective intensity, supporting the Entropic Brain theory.

papers.title: Examination of neurocognitive processes during execution of sequential problem-solving tasks under varying demand.
papers.summary: This study assessed behavioral performance and EEG spectral power during sequential problem-solving tasks with varying cognitive demand. Higher demand degraded performance and increased cortical recruitment leading to reduced neural efficiency, with best performers showing greater temporal and central beta/gamma power.

papers.title: Neurophysiological Signatures of Negative Symptom Improvement After High-Definition Transcranial Direct Current Stimulation: A Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation-Electroencephalography Study.
papers.summary: This randomized double-blind trial in schizophrenia patients found that 20 sessions of HD-tDCS targeting the left DLPFC improved negative symptoms and normalized N100 amplitude in TMS-EEG. N100 normalization was specifically associated with negative symptom improvement, suggesting restoration of cortical inhibition.

papers.title: Electroencephalographic Signatures of Methylphenidate in ADHD: A Systematic Review and 10 Recommendations for Future Research.
papers.summary: This systematic review of 44 studies examined EEG effects of methylphenidate in ADHD. The most consistent finding was increased P3 amplitude, but EEG did not meet criteria as a treatment-response biomarker.

papers.title: At-Home BCI Rehabilitation Therapy for Chronic Upper Extremity Deficit After Stroke (BCI-REHAB): A Randomized Trial.
papers.summary: This randomized trial compared at-home BCI therapy to at-home exercise for chronic stroke upper extremity deficit. The BCI group showed significantly greater improvement in Fugl-Meyer score (treatment difference 4.5 points) and higher response rate.

papers.title: Unlocking High-Fidelity Chemical NMR Spectral Information from Nonuniformly Sampled Experiments with Deep Learning.
papers.summary: This paper presents CLEAR, a physics-guided deep learning framework for reconstructing nonuniformly sampled NMR spectra. It achieved 16-25% lower reconstruction error compared to state-of-the-art methods, especially for weak peaks.

papers.title: Convergent Functional Connectivity Alterations in ADHD Revealed by EEG: A Systematic Review Across Methods, States and Spatial Scales.
papers.summary: This systematic review of 37 EEG functional connectivity studies in ADHD found convergent patterns of reduced posterior integration with frontal compensation, altered network interactions, and more local connectivity, paralleling fMRI findings.

papers.title: Multimodal EEG-HRV assessment of individual regulatory patterns: a perturbation-based approach toward precision psychiatry.
papers.summary: This pilot study used a perturbation-based EEG-HRV paradigm to assess cortico-autonomic regulation in 10 healthy participants. Findings showed high inter-individual variability, with coordinated changes in a subset, supporting feasibility for precision psychiatry.

papers.title: A high-rate 480-target hybrid BCI system based on SSVEP and sEMG.
papers.summary: This paper presents a hybrid BCI system combining SSVEP and sEMG to encode 480 targets using 120 flicker frequencies and 4 gestures. Online testing achieved 84.55% accuracy and an information transfer rate of 260.07 bits/min, demonstrating high-performance large-command-set capability.

papers.title: Motor Experience Does Not Uniformly Shape Attentional Flexibility: Behavioral and Neural Evidence.
papers.summary: The study examined attentional flexibility in table tennis athletes with different levels of motor experience using a spatial stimulus-response task and EEG. Results showed linear improvements in reaction time and accuracy with experience, but nonlinear EEG amplitude patterns for CNV and N2 components, indicating nonuniform neural changes.

papers.title: A Hybrid Signal Processing and Deep Learning Framework for Parkinson's Disease Classification and Determination of ON and OFF Medication Condition.
papers.summary: The paper presents a hybrid framework combining Variational Mode Decomposition and Wavelet Coherence with a 2D-CNN to classify Parkinson's disease and ON/OFF medication states from EEG signals. The model achieved high accuracy (99.80%) in classifying PD versus healthy controls, outperforming existing methods.

papers.title: Kindness Protects the Heart: The Positive Impact of Self-Compassion on Autobiographical Memory Retrieval.
papers.summary: This study examined how self-compassion affects autobiographical memory retrieval. High self-compassion individuals showed more specific memory retrieval and distinct neural processing, including larger late positive potentials and different theta-band network organization, compared to low self-compassion individuals.

papers.title: Preoperative Resting-State EEG Features Associated With Chronic Postoperative Pain After Breast Cancer Surgery: A Prospective Cohort Study.
papers.summary: This prospective cohort study of 84 breast cancer surgery patients found that preoperative resting-state EEG gamma-band power in frontal regions and gamma-band connectivity involving frontal, insular, and cingulate regions were higher in patients who developed chronic postoperative pain (NRS ≥ 4 at 3 months) compared to those with lower pain. Mastectomy and axillary lymph node dissection were also associated with higher pain risk.

papers.title: Continuous sliding pressure feedback enhances supernumerary robotic thumb proprioception over discrete vibrotactile feedback: Behavioral and EEG evidence.
papers.summary: This study compared continuous sliding pressure feedback and discrete vibrotactile feedback for conveying proprioceptive information from a supernumerary robotic thumb. Pressure feedback led to higher accuracy and more efficient neural integration (higher beta-band small-worldness), while vibrotactile feedback required more cortical processing.

papers.title: V-on-A Tachycardia Misclassified as Ventricular Tachycardia by Atrial Blanking: A 4-Question Electrogram Approach.
papers.summary: This case report describes a dual-chamber ICD misclassifying a short-VA supraventricular tachycardia as ventricular tachycardia due to atrial blanking. A 4-question electrogram analysis correctly identified typical AVNRT, preventing inappropriate therapy and guiding successful slow-pathway modification.

papers.title: Bonding before birth: Maternal-fetal attachment and maternal cortical connectivity in late pregnancy.
papers.summary: The study examined associations between resting-state EEG alpha coherence and maternal-fetal attachment in 35 third-trimester pregnant women. Higher left frontoparietal and intra-frontal alpha coherence was linked to greater anticipation and interaction aspects of attachment, even after controlling for parity and gestational age.

papers.title: Non-convulsive Status Epilepticus in L-2-Hydroxyglutaric Aciduria With a Novel L2HGDH Variant: A Case Report.
papers.summary: This case report describes a 29-year-old man with L-2-hydroxyglutaric aciduria presenting with non-convulsive status epilepticus, caused by a novel homozygous L2HGDH missense variant (c.191C>A, p.Ala64Asp). The report expands the seizure phenotype of L2HGA and highlights the role of molecular testing when biochemical findings are atypical.

papers.title: Save your friend, strike your enemy! How sex and handedness influence EEG signatures of cooperative and competitive behaviour.
papers.summary: The research tested evolutionary stable strategy predictions with EEG during Go/NoGo tasks involving cooperation (saving a friend) and competition (hitting an enemy) in left- and right-handed participants. Findings revealed sex and handedness effects on lateralization, with N2 latency and P3 amplitude patterns supporting some predictions.

papers.title: Relationship of early-onset sepsis and neonatal encephalopathy: early-onset sepsis can increase short-term adverse outcomes of neonatal encephalopathy.
papers.summary: This retrospective observational study of 87 neonates with mild neonatal encephalopathy found that those with concurrent early-onset sepsis had significantly higher rates of abnormal neurological examinations, seizures, abnormal EEG findings, antiepileptic medication use, and receipt of blood products compared to those without sepsis, indicating worse short-term outcomes.

papers.title: EEG Artifacts During Pediatric Cardiopulmonary Bypass: Three Illustrative Cases.
papers.summary: This paper reports three illustrative cases of EEG artifacts during pediatric cardiopulmonary bypass, highlighting their occurrence and potential sources. The cases likely demonstrate characteristic artifact patterns to aid in recognition and interpretation.

papers.title: An Evidence-Based Biomarker Framework for n-Hexane-Induced Neuropathy: Urinary 2,5-Hexanedione, Pyrrole Adducts, and Neurofilament Light Chain.
papers.summary: This review integrates toxicological and biomonitoring evidence for n-hexane-induced neuropathy, clarifying that urinary 2,5-hexanedione is an established exposure biomarker, pyrrole adducts are candidate toxicodynamic biomarkers, and neurofilament light chain is an exploratory axonal-injury biomarker with unequal validation maturity.

papers.title: Using the OPTIMAL Theory to Optimize Aerodynamics in Respiratory Training for Healthy Adults and Individuals With Parkinson's Disease.
papers.journal: International journal of language & communication disorders
papers.summary: This randomized controlled trial investigated whether applying OPTIMAL theory strategies during respiratory muscle strength training improves immediate respiratory motor performance in healthy adults and individuals with Parkinson's disease. Results showed significant improvements in peak expiratory flow in both OPTIMAL groups compared to controls, but no changes in cough strength.

papers.title: Murine ADAM15 Deficiency Is Associated With Atrial Remodelling and Atrial Arrhythmia Susceptibility.
papers.summary: This study examined the effects of ADAM15 deficiency on atrial biology in mice, finding increased atrial fibrillation susceptibility, shorter atrial action potential duration, increased fibrosis, increased TGFβ signaling, and reduced connexin expression. The findings implicate ADAM15 in atrial remodeling and arrhythmia susceptibility.

papers.title: Longitudinal Evidence on Natural History, Nonoperative Management, and Multimodal Surveillance in Mild to Moderate Degenerative Cervical Myelopathy: A Scoping Review.
papers.summary: This scoping review maps longitudinal evidence on natural history, nonoperative management, and multimodal surveillance in mild to moderate degenerative cervical myelopathy. Findings suggest that mild to moderate disease is not uniformly stable, and multimodal follow-up appears more informative than single-scale monitoring.

papers.title: Rapid Whole-Plant Signalling Under Compound Environmental Stresses: Systemic Integration, Stomatal Coordination and Stress Memory.
papers.summary: This review develops a mechanistic framework for rapid whole-plant signaling under compound environmental stresses, emphasizing multi-speed signaling via ROS, Ca2+, electrical, and hydraulic waves, with a focus on stomatal coordination. It identifies unresolved questions and outlines an experimental pipeline combining biosensors, electrophysiology, and spatial omics to link dynamic signals to acclimation outcomes.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
